objective.statement: Write the scales and key signature of G flat major and E flat minor.
successCriteria: I know both keys have six flats and are relative to each other.
I spell each scale with every letter used once, including C flat.
I know G flat major and F sharp major sound the same.

explanation.text: G♭ major has six flats (B♭ E♭ A♭ D♭ G♭ C♭), and so does its relative minor, E♭ minor. They are the enharmonic twins of F♯ major and D♯ minor: the same scales on the piano, spelt with flats instead of sharps. Use whichever spelling the question names; they are never interchangeable in an answer.

music.textAlternative: The scale of G flat major, ascending: G♭ A♭ B♭ C♭ D♭ E♭ F G♭.

explanation.caption: G♭ major: the fourth note is C♭, not B, and the leading note is F natural.

explanation.text: Spell by letters again: G A B C D E F G, then flats from the signature. The fourth note is C♭ (it would sound like B, but the letter must be C). The leading note, F, needs no flat, because the key signature does not flatten it.

music.textAlternative: The harmonic minor scale of E flat, ascending: E♭ F G♭ A♭ B♭ C♭ D E♭.

explanation.caption: E♭ harmonic minor: the seventh note, D♭ in the signature, is raised to D natural.

explanation.text: In E♭ minor the harmonic form raises the seventh, D♭, to D♮. The melodic form raises both the sixth (C♭ becomes C♮) and the seventh going up, and restores them coming down. Remember: an accidental in front of a note changes only that note, and only until the end of the bar.
Six flats: B E A D G C. Each letter once in the scale. C♭ and B sound the same, but only C♭ is spelt correctly in G♭ major.

music.textAlternative: The first four notes of G flat major: G♭ A♭ B♭ C♭.

steps: All are flat in this key.
